_about: Astro Precise — the £2.99 Eclipse Night Reading. Honest template library. The engine computes WHERE the 12 Aug 2026 eclipse degree falls against a person's real natal chart; these templates turn that computed contact into words. TYPE LAW: the 'computed' line is fact (render in mono); the 'reflection' line is human meaning (render in warm serif). Everything traditional is framed as reflection, never prediction. Nothing here is fabricated — every number the engine drops in is real; the words only interpret it. Legal 'for reflection/entertainment' line ships with every reading.
voice: Calm, specific, grown-up. Fact first, then a gentle traditional meaning offered for reflection. No promises about health, money or love. No 'you will'. No fear.
legalLine: Astronomy is exact; the meaning is tradition, offered for reflection and entertainment — not advice or prediction.

reflectionFrames.conjunction: This eclipse falls right on {theme}. Eclipses have long been read as endings that clear a little space for a beginning — so this is a moment to notice what here feels ready to turn over.
reflectionFrames.opposition: This eclipse sits directly opposite {theme}. Tradition reads a facing like this as a call for balance — a nudge to see this part of you from the other side.
reflectionFrames.square: This eclipse presses on {theme}. A square is old shorthand for useful friction — the kind of tension that, handled gently, tends to move something that was stuck.
reflectionFrames.trine: This eclipse flows easily with {theme}. A trine is the kind, unforced contact — a good moment to lean on this strength rather than force anything.
reflectionFrames.sextile: This eclipse gently opens {theme}. A helpful angle is a small door, not a shove — an invitation you can take or leave.

overrides.sun|conjunction: This eclipse falls right on your Sun — your core sense of who you are. Of all the contacts, this is the personal one: a traditional marker of a chapter quietly closing so a truer one can begin. Held lightly, it's an invitation to ask what you've outgrown.
overrides.moon|conjunction: This eclipse falls right on your Moon — your inner tides and what makes you feel safe. Tradition treats this as a tender, emotional reset; be a little gentler with yourself around it than you'd think to be.
overrides.asc|conjunction: This eclipse falls right on your Ascendant — the face you meet the world with. It's read, traditionally, as a moment when how you show up is ready to shift; nobody else has to notice for it to be real.
overrides.saturn|conjunction: This eclipse meets your Saturn — your patience and your load. The old reading isn't heavy: it's a moment to set down one thing you've been carrying out of habit rather than need.

emptyState.computed: The eclipse point sits more than {maxOrb}° from every placement in your chart — no close contact tonight.
emptyState.computedNoHard: No placement in your chart takes a direct hit from this eclipse: nothing of yours sits within {maxOrb}° of the eclipse point, or directly opposite it, or square to it.
emptyState.nearestSoft: There is a softer touch nearby — the eclipse point {frame} your {targetLabel}, {orbText} away. That contact is real; it is just a gentle one, and we would rather name it than build a night on it.
emptyState.nearestWide: The nearest contact of any kind is {orbText} from your {targetLabel} — real, and too wide to carry a night.
emptyState.reflection: So this one is quiet for you, and quiet is a real reading. Charts are not scored out of ten; the sky simply doesn't reach everybody on the same night, and plenty of places would happily sell you a reading anyway. You still get the eclipse over your own town and the Perseids after dark — and your chart is no less yours for sitting this one out.

perseid.computed: After the eclipse, the Perseids peak overnight — your darkest window is roughly {darkStart}–{darkEnd}, radiant climbing in the north-east.
perseid.reflection: An old, unserious tradition worth keeping: the first shooting star you catch is yours to make a wish on.

shareLine: The eclipse landed {orbText} from my {targetLabel}. Check where it falls in yours →

questions.sun: So the question tonight is a quiet one: which version of you is asking to be lived openly now — and what have you outgrown?
questions.moon: So the question the sky hands you is not 'what should you want?' but the quieter one underneath: what do you actually need, before anyone told you what you were supposed to?
questions.mercury: So the question tonight: what is waiting to be said plainly — and to whom?
questions.venus: So the question tonight: what do you love that you have been treating as optional?
questions.mars: So the question tonight: where is your effort going out of habit rather than choice?
questions.jupiter: So the question tonight: where are you being invited to grow — and what small door have you not opened?
questions.saturn: So the question tonight: which load are you carrying out of habit that was never yours to keep?
questions.uranus: So the question tonight: where does your life ask for more room than you have given it?
questions.neptune: So the question tonight: which dream have you been calling unrealistic mainly because it matters?
questions.pluto: So the question tonight: what is quietly ending so something truer can take its place?
questions.asc: So the question tonight: does the way you meet the world still fit the person doing the meeting?
questions.mc: So the question tonight: is the direction you are walking still the one you would choose today?

close.computedPerseids: The same night, the Perseids peak — up to {rate} meteors an hour after midnight, the radiant climbing in the north-east; your darkest window is roughly {darkStart}–{darkEnd}.
close.computedNoPerseids: After the eclipse the sky stays busy — step outside and let it be enough.
close.serif: You don't have to answer any of this tonight. A page is turning; you're allowed to simply go and watch it turn.

secondary.serif: Quieter touches, worth a glance — the closest contact above is the one that carries the night.

quietGate.note: UI RULE (binding): when quiet:true, the buyer must SEE the quiet verdict before paying — the empty state gates the sale, never surprises after it.
